A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite the changed title and terminology. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v3 affect interpretation of particular additions, rather than material completeness.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer-training experiments, representation analyses, activation interventions, finetuning and prompting results, and OLMo checkpoint evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds mixed-regression, attention-head pruning, bitwise OLMo pretraining, and non-transformer model results.

M1.justification: The core encoding-decoding framework, kNN decodability measure, and retained patching, finetuning, and prompting procedures remain substantively unchanged. Renaming concept decodability to task decodability and expanding its implementation description do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: v3 adds a heterogeneous regression experiment covering linear, sparse linear, leaky-ReLU, and quadratic functions in Section 3.3 and Figure 16, substantially extending v1's sparse-regression task coverage. POS and bitwise tasks remain. Appendix F inconsistently names cubic and sinusoidal regression, leaving the exact added setup partly uncertain.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same least-squares and weighted-Lasso reference curves. The finetuning and prompting experiments retain their pretrained, first-ten-layer, last-ten-layer, and prompted comparison conditions. Added model evaluations test the framework's generality without introducing a competing method.

E3.justification: v3 adds individual attention-head pruning evaluated on 100 random sequences per basis or regression family, and extends evaluation beyond transformer architectures. These are substantive additions to the evaluation design. The exact new architecture is unresolved: Section 4.3 and Figure 22 identify Mamba, whereas Appendix G.4 specifies a two-layer LSTM with 512 hidden units per layer.

E4.justification: New mixed-family and head-pruning analyses investigate when tasks share computational machinery versus require distinct representations and heads. These substantially extend v1's activation-patching and overlapping-basis analyses. Conversely, v1 Figure 7's finetuning decodability-by-layer curves and representation UMAP are removed; v3 supplies aggregate summaries instead.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 5 newly shows standard-deviation shading across tasks, and Table 1 adds plus/minus summaries without clearly defining their spread measure. Both versions already report five synthetic-training seeds and five intervention replicates; an increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: v3 adds mixed-regression and pruning results, OLMo bitwise trajectories, and Figure 22 correlations of R-squared 0.468 for bitwise arithmetic and 0.596 for POS. Table 1 newly tabulates finetuning and prompting aggregates. Existing Llama/Gemma performance plots are largely retained. Section 4.1 also reassigns v1's POS/arithmetic intervention averages to separable/overlapping task groups despite retaining the intervention plots.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated unidentified-basis error behavior from approaching zero between r and D demonstrations in v1 to approaching zero with D demonstrations in v3. The Bayesian equation and appendix regression argument remain. The expanded kNN accuracy formula primarily explains the existing metric; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims of coupled encoding-decoding emergence and decodability predicting ICL performance remain. The abstract and introduction narrow the novelty framing from proposing an abstraction mechanism to using an encoder-decoder framework to explain task vectors, while giving previously reported pretraining and early-layer finetuning findings greater prominence.

C2.justification: v3 extends the shared-algorithm interpretation to successful mixed-family regression without separable task vectors, adds explanations for gradual LLM pretraining dynamics and possible generalization beyond transformers, and removes the broader activation-steering discussion. Appendix F contradicts the new nonseparability interpretation by claiming clear separation. Existing multistep-reasoning limitations and the prompting-confound caveat remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents Figure 2's UMAP sampling and parameters, selection of the layer maximizing TD, leave-one-out kNN classification, and an activation-patching recipe in Appendix C. Most existing training, LoRA, hardware, and runtime details are retained. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the corresponding existing procedures.

R1.justification: v3 adds a contrast with Park et al.'s homogeneous Markov-chain setting, positions early-layer finetuning against Wu et al. and Kumar et al., and adds recurrent-model references. It replaces the prompting citation to Wei et al. with Liu et al. The main Bayesian, task-vector, and interpretability foundations remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statements, terminology, and substantial experimental prose are rewritten around task vectors and TD. Related-work subsections are merged, pretraining receives a main-text subsection, finetuning material moves into a dedicated appendix, and the discussion is reorganized. This exceeds simple renaming or added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, combines UMAP and decodability panels, relocates several existing figures, removes v1 Figure 7, and adds Table 1 and new experimental plots. New display inconsistencies are substantive: Figure 16 describes a TD curve as a UMAP, and Figures 17–18 have captions that reverse the experiments identified inside their panels.

improvement.justification: v3 offers broader mechanistic tests, clearer metric documentation, and useful aggregate summaries. However, its principal additions contain unresolved contradictions: Section 3.3 and Appendix F disagree on regression families and representation separation, Appendix G.4 names an LSTM while Figure 22 names Mamba, and pruning captions reverse the displayed experiments. These problems obscure what the added evidence establishes, preventing a reliable net quality judgment relative to v1.
